resources.barrier_detail: No barrier. REST API https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/ws/archive/v2/search/projects?keyword=... returned HTTP 200 on every one of the 59 queries. Full pagination (pageSize=100, page=0..n) also HTTP 200. Detail endpoint /v2/projects/<acc> HTTP 200. One API quirk, NOT an access barrier: /v2/files/byProject?accession=<acc> returns HTTP 200 with a zero-byte body (size_download:0) for every accession tried; the v3 equivalent /v3/projects/<acc>/files?pageSize=200 returns HTTP 200 with full JSON, so file manifests were obtained via v3.
resources.notes: DECISIVE NEGATIVE FOR THE ACTUAL ENDPOINT. I paginated the complete result sets and intersected them locally rather than trusting single queries: keyword 'platelet' = 432 projects; union of 'oligonucleotide'(197) + 'antisense'(156) + 'siRNA'(379) = 659 projects. The accession intersection is 3, and all 3 are coincidental, not oligonucleotide-exposed platelets: PXD035018 (human primary macrophages + LNA target-site blockers; carries organismPart 'Blood platelet' BTO:0000132 as a stray annotation - the study profiles macrophages, platelets are never assayed), PXD037158 (mouse thrombospondin-1 trafficking TO platelets, no oligonucleotide), PXD063570 (rat CNS myelin, irrelevant). A separate regex scan of title+description+keywords of all 659 oligo-matching projects for platelet|thrombocyt|megakaryocyt|GPVI|glycoprotein VI|PF4|platelet factor 4|P-selectin|thrombus|GP6 returned exactly 1 project (PXD037158, incidental). Intersection of 'thrombocytopenia'(21) with the oligo union = 0. Every named priority drug returns n=0: oblimersen, G3139, mipomersen, drisapersen, aprinocarsen, alicaforsen, pelacarsen, olezarsen, donidalorsen, inclisiran, fomivirsen, eteplirsen, golodirsen, viltolarsen, casimersen, tofersen. Only nusinersen matched (n=6), all cerebrospinal-fluid biomarker studies, no platelet measurement. CONCLUSION: as of 2026-10-02 PRIDE contains NO platelet or megakaryocyte proteomics dataset acquired under oligonucleotide exposure, and no deposition attached to any thrombocytopenia-associated oligonucleotide trial. The 9 datasets reported above are a DIFFERENT, secondary category: human in vitro oligonucleotide protein-interaction / chemistry-comparator and oligonucleotide-safety proteomics. They do not contain platelet counts or platelet activation readouts and cannot close the thrombocytopenia endpoint; they are useful only as backbone-chemistry and protein-binding mechanism anchors. Note that the challenge-relevant GPVI hit (PXD046982) involves Affimer protein reagents, NOT oligonucleotides. PRIDE's keyword index does search projectDescription (it returned projects whose only match was in the abstract), so these negatives are not an artifact of a title-only index.

resources.barrier_detail: No access barrier. Note: http://proteomecentral.proteomexchange.org/api/proxi/v0.1/datasets (the plain-HTTP form given in the task guidance) returns HTTP 301 Moved Permanently from nginx/1.24.0 (Ubuntu). Re-issuing over HTTPS with redirect-follow (https://proteomecentral.proteomexchange.org/api/proxi/v0.1/datasets?keywords=...&resultType=compact) returns HTTP 200 with a JSON body whose status block reads {'status':'OK','status_code':200}. All 24 queries returned HTTP 200. The endpoint is slow (single queries took tens of seconds; a 13-query batch exceeded a 120s foreground limit and had to be run as a background job), but nothing timed out at the 110s per-request cap.
resources.notes: APPLICABLE BUT A MUCH WEAKER INDEX THAN PRIDE, which materially limits what a negative here proves on its own. PROXI's 'keywords' parameter matches only the submitter-supplied keyword list, not the title or description: 'platelet' returns 15 datasets here versus 432 in PRIDE, 'platelet proteome' and 'glycoprotein VI' return 0 here while returning 36 and 5 in PRIDE, and 'phosphorothioate' returns 0 here despite PRIDE holding 6. I therefore treat PRIDE as the primary evidence for the negative and PROXI only as cross-repository coverage. PROXI's value is that it spans repositories PRIDE does not: it surfaced 2 datasets my PRIDE keyword sweep never saw - PXD082807 (jPOST; human immortalized megakaryocyte imMKCL proteomics fractionated by cell size and culture duration, submitter keyword 'artificial platelets') and PXD031432 (PanoramaPublic; human+rat PrP LC-MRM-MS from antisense oligonucleotide work). It also independently confirmed the central negative: zero overlap between oligonucleotide terms and platelet/thrombocytopenia terms across PRIDE, MassIVE, iProX, jPOST and PanoramaPublic. 'thrombocytopenia' = 0 datasets repository-wide. 'oblimersen', 'mipomersen', 'eteplirsen', 'P-selectin', 'platelet factor 4', 'morpholino' all = 0. No MassIVE or iProX platelet dataset involves oligonucleotide exposure (the iProX platelet entries are homocysteine-treated mouse platelets, mouse ischemic-stroke platelets, and human sepsis platelets). I did NOT find and do not claim any platelet-proteomics-under-oligonucleotide dataset in any ProteomeXchange partner repository.

notes:
SCOPE: proteomics resource family only - PRIDE Archive and ProteomeXchange/ProteomeCentral. Search date 2026-10-02. Both resources were genuinely searched; neither was blocked; no login, CAPTCHA, paywall or credential was encountered or required, and nothing was purchased. No authors were contacted. 83 real queries ran in total (59 PRIDE + 24 PROXI), all HTTP 200.

HEADLINE, STATED PLAINLY: the proteomics family does NOT close the oligonucleotide-induced thrombocytopenia endpoint, and I found no dataset that does. As of 2026-10-02 there is NO platelet or megakaryocyte proteomics dataset acquired under oligonucleotide exposure in PRIDE, and none in any ProteomeXchange partner repository (PRIDE, MassIVE, iProX, jPOST, PanoramaPublic). This is a tested negative, not an untested assumption: I paginated the full PRIDE result sets (432 platelet-matching projects, 659 in the oligonucleotide/antisense/siRNA union) and intersected accessions locally, finding 3 coincidental overlaps and zero genuine ones; a regex scan of all 659 oligonucleotide-matching project titles, descriptions and keywords for platelet terms returned a single incidental mouse hit. The thrombocytopenia x oligonucleotide intersection is empty in both resources.

APPLICABILITY JUDGEMENT, as the guidance asked: the family is APPLICABLE IN PRINCIPLE and I am not recording it as not_applicable. Both halves are richly populated independently - human platelet proteomics is well represented (PRIDE 'platelet proteome' n=36, including Glanzmann thrombasthenia, essential thrombocythemia, myeloproliferative neoplasm and ultra-sensitive platelet proteome studies) and oligonucleotide proteomics is well represented - but the intersection that this endpoint needs has never been deposited. The guidance anticipated GPVI/PF4 interaction studies as the likely hit; the GPVI dataset does exist (PXD046982) but uses Affimer protein reagents, not oligonucleotides, and I have flagged that prominently rather than letting it read as a hit.

WHAT THE 11 CANDIDATES ACTUALLY ARE: none is platelet-plus-oligonucleotide. They fall in three honest tiers. (1) Human in vitro oligonucleotide protein-interaction and chemistry-comparator datasets, priority 2 - PXD068788, PXD070121, PXD045992, PXD065583, and at priority 3 PXD066763 and PXD079777. These matter because phosphorothioate protein promiscuity is the accepted upstream mechanism of ASO platelet activation, and these give per-replicate, backbone- and 2'-modification-resolved measurements of that property in human cells. PXD068788 is the strongest: one SSO sequence on tcDNA, LNA and 2'MOE backbones plus two TSB controls, 5 biological replicates each, with raw per-replicate data and an open sample key. (2) Structural and clinical context, priority 3 - PXD046982 (human GPVI HDX-MS, no oligonucleotide), PXD055796 (human BIIB078 ALS trial spinal cord), PXD031432. (3) Comparator scaffolds carrying zero oligonucleotide observations, priority 3 - PXD082807 (human imMKCL megakaryocyte baseline) and PXD006559 (human ex vivo platelet activation baseline). Tier 3 must not be curated as oligonucleotide evidence; it is included only so the dataset builder knows what reference proteomes exist.

PRIORITY-TARGET COVERAGE: of the named priority compounds, PRIDE and PROXI hold depositions for NONE except nusinersen. Searched and returned n=0 in both: oblimersen/G3139/Genasense, drisapersen, aprinocarsen/ISIS 3521, alicaforsen/ISIS 2302, pelacarsen, olezarsen, donidalorsen, mipomersen, inclisiran, fomivirsen, eteplirsen, golodirsen, viltolarsen, casimersen, tofersen. ISIS 5132 was not separately queryable as a distinct term beyond the generic phosphorothioate and antisense sweeps, which it did not surface. Nusinersen returned 6 PRIDE projects, all cerebrospinal-fluid biomarker studies (PXD065345, PXD054900, PXD016757 among them) with no platelet measurement, so they do not address NURTURE, SHINE or DEVOTE platelet values. Neither resource holds anything from Sewing 2017 or Slingsby 2022, and neither holds the cASO sequences themselves - PXD070121 is that paper's proteomics arm, and the sequences remain in its article supplement, already staged by this project's literature sweep.

STAGED FILE (one, legally open): pride_PXD068788_Corresponding_names.pdf, 132481 bytes, sha256 6d23be917d426a2d88fe8285cf411b2e88ce20f088df2795e19bf91902daaa5c, retrieved HTTP 200 from https://ftp.pride.ebi.ac.uk/pride/data/archive/2026/01/PXD068788/Corresponding_names.pdf, written to /home/user/oligos/thrombocytopenia/curation/research_staging/. It is the PXD068788 sample key mapping each .d raw file to its publication sample name, confirming the 6-condition x 5-biological-replicate design and the tcDNA/LNA/2'MOE chemistry assignment per run. I deliberately did NOT download the bulk processed archives (PXD068788 results.zip 251 MB; PXD070121 DIANN1.9.2.zip 1.85 GB) - they are openly reachable by the FTP URLs recorded above and can be fetched on demand, but neither contains platelet data and pulling 2 GB into staging was not warranted.

IDENTIFIER VERIFICATION: every PMID, PMCID and DOI reported here was resolved through the Europe PMC REST API (HTTP 200) rather than recalled - PMID 42733805/PMC13571576, 41630988/PMC12860984, 38233583/PMC11062921, 38838227/PMC11321386, 41918821/PMC13034028, 37701067/PMC10494319, all isOpenAccess=Y. Where a PRIDE record carries no publication reference (PXD079777) or where I read a DOI from the PRIDE record without independently resolving a PMID (PXD066763 doi:10.1038/s41467-025-64434-7, PXD055796 doi:10.1016/j.cell.2025.07.045), I report exactly that and invent nothing. No NCT numbers are claimed from this family because neither resource exposes trial registrations, so no ClinicalTrials.gov verification was applicable.

TWO API CAVEATS WORTH PASSING ON, neither an access barrier. First, PRIDE's v2 /files/byProject endpoint returns HTTP 200 with a ZERO-BYTE body for every accession tried; file manifests require the v3 endpoint /v3/projects/<acc>/files. Second and more important for interpreting negatives, ProteomeXchange PROXI's keywords parameter matches ONLY the submitter-supplied keyword list, not titles or descriptions: it returned 15 datasets for 'platelet' against PRIDE's 432, and 0 for 'platelet proteome', 'glycoprotein VI' and 'phosphorothioate' where PRIDE returned 36, 5 and 6. A PROXI zero therefore proves much less than a PRIDE zero, which is why I rested the central negative on PRIDE and used PROXI only for cross-repository reach. That reach was real: PROXI surfaced PXD082807 (jPOST), PXD031432 (PanoramaPublic) and PXD055796, which my PRIDE keyword queries never returned. Also note the plain-HTTP PROXI URL in the task guidance returns HTTP 301 from nginx and must be re-issued over HTTPS, and that the endpoint is slow enough that a 13-query batch exceeded a 120-second foreground limit and had to be backgrounded. One background wait job was stopped on reaching its time limit; its query batch had already completed and its results are fully recorded above, so nothing was lost.

RECOMMENDATION: do not spend further effort on proteomics repositories for the platelet endpoint - the intersection is empty and I have tested it directly from both sides. The family's residual value is the chemistry-comparator tier, above all PXD068788, which is human, in vitro, per-replicate and backbone-resolved, and therefore sits well with the Phase 2 preference even though it measures protein binding rather than platelet count.
